'''Roger Wolcott Richardson''' (30 May 1930 &ndash; 15 June 1993) was a mathematician noted for his work in [[representation theory]] and [[geometry]]. 

== Life ==
Richardson was born in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]], and educated at [[Louisiana State University]], [[Harvard University]] and [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor]] where he obtained a [[Ph.D.]] in 1958 under the supervision of [[Hans Samelson]]. After a postdoc appointment at [[Princeton University]], he accepted a faculty position at the [[University of Washington]] in [[Seattle]]. He emigrated to the [[United Kingdom]] in 1970, taking up a chair at [[Durham University]]. In 1978 he moved to the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]], where he stayed as faculty until his death.

Richardson's best known result states that if ''P'' is a [[Borel subgroup|parabolic subgroup]] of a [[reductive group]], then ''P'' has a dense orbit on its [[Nilradical of a Lie algebra|nilradical]], i.e., one whose closure is the whole space.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1112/blms/6.1.21|doi=10.1112/blms/6.1.21|title=Conjugacy Classes in Parabolic Subgroups of Semisimple Algebraic Groups|year=1974|last1=Richardson|first1=R. W.|journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|volume=6|pages=21–24|url-access=subscription}}</ref> This orbit is now universally known as the [[Richardson orbit]].<ref>Gus I. Lehrer, ''[https://www.science.org.au/files/userfiles/fellowship/memoirs/documents/richards.pdf Roger Wolcott Richardson 1930–1993]'', Historical Records of Australian Science, Volume 11 Number 4 (1997)</ref>

He was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Roger Richardson |url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/roger-richardson |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en}}</ref>

In 1997 the [[Cambridge University Press]] published ''Algebraic Groups and Lie Groups: A Volume of Papers in Honour of the Late R. W. Richardson'', which was organized by a committee of 5 mathematicians selected by the [[Australian Mathematical Society]]. The volume's preface has several paragraphs about Richardson's research.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Lehrer, G. I.|title=Algebraic Groups and Lie Groups: A Volume of Papers in Honour of the Late R. W. Richardson|series=Lecture Series, Volume 9, Australian Mathematical Society|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1997|isbn=0521585325|lccn=96038843|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=es9VNGJHOaEC}}</ref>
